text:
Aaron Ekblad is 30, a first overall pick, a Calder winner and a two-time Stanley Cup champion, and on the evidence of this season he's playing his best five-on-five hockey in a while. Florida takes 60% of the expected goals with him on the ice, nearly 13 points better than without him. That's an elite number on any team.

It's a sharp turn from a year ago, when Evolving-Hockey had him around replacement level with opponents getting more chances against him than almost any defenseman (bottom 7%). Nineteen games don't erase a season, but the direction is clear.

The points are steady (eight in 19, two assists in Columbus on Nov. 10, another in the comeback against Detroit), and his shooting at 3.7% is below normal, so a goal or two is owed. He's playing 21 minutes a night, roughly where he's been. What we'd watch is whether the five-on-five numbers hold as the schedule tightens. If they do, Florida has its top-pair righty back.
